record.original_question: Does every nonnegative integer eventually appear in the Recamán sequence a_0=0, a_n=a_{n-1}-n when that value is positive and new, and a_n=a_{n-1}+n otherwise?

evidence.quote: It is not a permutation of the integers since a_20 = 42 = a_24. Sloane conjectured that each number will eventually appear in the sequence but this is not known.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define a sequence of nonnegative integers $(a_n)_{n\ge 0}$ by $a_0 = 0$ and, for $n \ge 1$,
\[
a_n = \begin{cases} a_{n-1} - n & \text{if } a_{n-1} - n > 0 \text{ and } a_{n-1} - n \notin \{a_0, a_1, \dots, a_{n-1}\},\\ a_{n-1} + n & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}
\]
Prove or disprove: for every nonnegative integer $m$ there exists an index $n$ with $a_n = m$.
artifact.status_search_result: Sloane's conjecture that every nonnegative integer eventually appears in the Recamán sequence (OEIS A005132) is a well-known open problem. The OEIS entry and various references state the conjecture remains unproven; computational searches have verified appearance for many small integers but the smallest missing value (currently 852,655 or similar large numbers depending on date of computation) has not been shown to appear.

status_evidence.title: OEIS A005132 - Recamán's sequence
status_evidence.snippet: Sloane conjectures that every number eventually appears, but this is not known.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is recorded as open on the OEIS page for the Recamán sequence.
